cards.front: Which characters may a Java identifier start with?
cards.back: A Unicode letter, an underscore _, or a dollar sign $
cards.extra: Digits and symbols such as - cannot start an identifier; after the first character digits are allowed. The language rule is broader than a beginner summary suggests: any letter Character.isJavaIdentifierStart accepts counts, including non-Latin scripts and currency symbols.

cards.back: An identifier cannot start with a digit
cards.extra: The compiler reads 1stPlace as a numeric literal followed by junk. Same for -total, which parses as an operator.

cards.back: Reserved words with a fixed meaning that cannot be used as identifiers
cards.extra: class, int, new, if. You cannot redefine them, which is why class cannot name a variable.

cards.front: How does the compiler treat whitespace?
cards.back: As a separator only — any run of spaces, tabs or line breaks counts as one
cards.extra: int age and int\nage compile identically. Whitespace matters only when it separates tokens; inside a string literal it is data.

cards.front: What is the difference between // and /* */ comments?
cards.back: // comments to the end of the line; /* */ spans lines and must be closed
cards.extra: An unclosed block comment swallows the rest of the file into a compile error. Block comments also cannot nest.
Consequences: string is not String, and a typo in capitalisation is a compile error, not a silent bug.
